Meeting Point: We will meet directly outside the front doors of the Redmond Library (15990 NE 85th St, Redmond), the entrance facing the parking lot. There is a small plaza area there where everyone can gather comfortably before we head across the street to connect to the trail.

  * Trip Accessibility: 1A. Fully paved, flat, and level trail. Total distance will be roughly 1.5 to 2 miles walking at a very gentle, slow pace focused on mindful observation.
  * Parking: Plenty of free parking is available in the Redmond Library parking lot, including ADA-accessible spots.
  * Bathrooms: Restrooms are available inside the library during operating hours.


Join us for a Mindful Birding Walk along the Sammamish River Trail!

Slow down, engage your senses, and connect with the local autumn environment on this gentle morning walk. Starting from the Redmond Library, we will quickly connect to the Sammamish River Trail, which offers a beautiful, open riparian habitat transitioning into its October foliage.

This walk is designed to be a mindful, slow-paced experience where we practice deep listening and observational awareness. The trail is completely paved and flat, making it highly accessible and a wonderful option for birders of all experience levels. Because this habitat blends river ecology with open brush and parkland, we will keep our eyes and ears open for resident and autumn-migrating species. We can expect to see or hear a variety of waterfowl and herons by the water, resident songbirds like song sparrows, black-capped chickadees, and cedar waxwings, as well as raptors hunting overhead as the seasonal shifts settle in.

Please bring binoculars if you have them, water, and comfortable walking shoes. No dogs, please, to help us keep a quiet and attentive presence for the birds.

This October, join us for an Island adventure as our next Birding Vacation takes on Orcas Island! Why visit the San Juans in October, you say? Fall is known by locals as the most magical time of year in its slower pace, gorgeous autumn colors, crisp morning air, and plenty of opportunities for viewing returning migrant shorebirds and waterfowl!

It doesn't get more Pacific Northwest than this: a ferry ride through the San Juans, lodging at the charming Outlook Inn located in the heart of cozy Eastsound, quiet mornings spent spotting Pacific Loons at North Beach, birds eye perspective of the island as we enjoy lunch from the top of Mount Constitution, afternoons spent adventuring through the diverse habitats the Island has to offer, then topping it all off with delicious dinners at independent eateries featuring island sourced produce!

title: Field Trip: Billy Frank Jr. Nisqually National Wildlife Refuge
description:
Click here to register for this trip! https://secure.birdsconnectsea.org/a/nisquallyoct2026

Meet: 6:30 AM Green Lake (Ravenna) P&R. South side of North lot near 65th St.

Limit: 12

Trip Accessibility: 1 (leisurely pace), B (mostly soft ground trails and boardwalk), ~3 miles walking

October 10, 2026 is World Mental Health Day and World Migratory Bird Day. As science has proved time and again lately that getting outside and looking at birds provides a number of mental health benefits, what better excuse to get outside and go birding together as we welcome back our winter birds!

Additionally, October 10, 2026 is the October Big Day. Over the course of 24 hours, the birding world unites in a common goal to observe, record, and celebrate the avian diversity around us. Come join us!

Billy Frank Jr. Nisqually National Wildlife Refuge includes a combination of estuaries, tide flats, freshwater marshes, woodlands, and grasslands. The Nisqually Delta is a major non-coastal resting and feeding area for migrating birds and there are few places in the region better for observing them. We will walk the forest and barn trails and go as far out on the boardwalk as we care to go. This event involves several miles of walking on good, flat trails with restroom opportunities at the start and mid-way.

We'll spend about 4 hours in the field. Pack snacks, lunch and water. Dress for wind and rain. Bring layers, rain gear, water and snacks. Carpool fees are 65 cents per mile per BCS guidelines, to be divided by passengers in each car. Sliding scale available. Return 1-2PM, depending on traffic.

title: Field Trip: Practice Birding by Ear in Westcrest Park
description:
Click here to register for this trip! https://secure.birdsconnectsea.org/a/oct26westcrest

Meet: 8:00AM, Playground Parking Lot, on 8th Ave SW between SW Trenton St. and SW Cloverdale St. Bus #131 stops at 9th Ave SW and SW Trenton St, then it’s less than 10 minutes to walk to the parking lot.

Limit: 12

Trip Accessibility: 1 (leisurely pace), C (sidewalks plus hiking trails with gentle rolling hills plus a few sets of stairs), approx. 1.5 miles walking

Westcrest Park is the southern end of the West Duwamish Greenbelt and includes trails winding through mixed forest, a community garden, and open greenspace over the covered water reservoir. Anyone interested in birds is welcome – the trip leaders will have extra pairs of binoculars for folks who need them. Our route will first meander south through the open space and return via the trees to include different sorts of habitat. We'll likely encounter Bewick's and Pacific Wrens, Ruby-crowned and Golden-crowned Kinglets, Spotted Towhees, Red-breasted Nuthatches, Song Sparrows, American Robins. Perhaps Hutton's Vireo. Pileated Woodpeckers, Cooper's Hawks, and Common Ravens are always possible. A significant portion of the walk lends itself to finding birds by their sounds, because the tree canopy is high. We expect to end around 11am--our route usually takes about 3 hours, depending on what we see and hear and how many questions spark conversation.

title: Community Speaker Series: Owls of Seattle with Ed Dominguez
description:
REGISTER https://secure.birdsconnectsea.org/a/speakerseries-owlsinseattle-dominguez

Date/Time: Thursday, October 15, 2026, 6:30pm

Location: Birds Connect Seattle (616 Olive Way)

Seattle is home to several species of owls. These mysterious birds have sparked the imagination of humans for millennia. We will explore the myth, folklore, and science of these hunter of the night. Discover where they can be found, how they are successful as nocturnal predators, and their importance to us in a variety of ways.

This in-person event will not be live-streamed or recorded.

Ticket fees help support Birds Connect Seattle's mission to advocate and organize for cities where people and birds thrive. Tickets are non-refundable.

Ed Dominguez is a Pacific Northwest Naturalist, who has been an educator and outdoor leader for over 30 years. For many years he was best known for his role as Lead Naturalist at the Seward Park Audubon Center in Seattle. After retiring from that role in 2025, Ed has continued his commitment to educating and spreading love for the natural world by leading private tours, offering speaking engagements and volunteering with Birds Connect Seattle. You can find him leading monthly walks at Union Bay Natural Area, as well as helping guide our Birding Vacations program. Ed is a natural born teacher, who wants to inspire folks to get outdoors and engage their curiosity about the natural world. Spending time with Ed, you'll expand your understanding of many different topics, such as conservation, local owls, botany, geology and natural history.

title: Planning for the Future: Making a Gift for Birds Through Your Will
description:
Have you ever thought about how you can support the causes you care about for generations to come? Join Birds Connect Seattle for a casual presentation and conversation about wills, estate planning, and the many ways you can include charitable giving in your plans.

You'll learn the basics of making a gift to Birds Connect Seattle through your will, including different types of bequests, sample language you can share with your attorney, and answers to common questions. title: In-Person Class: Mobile Sketching Across the Skagit and Samish Flats with Carleen O. Zimmerman
description:
This class is at capacity. Register for the WAITLIST. https://secure.birdsconnectsea.org/a/mobilesketching2026

Field sketching is not scientific illustration but rather a way to create visual memories of birding habitats where we might see or hear birds. Often your best birding adventures happen when you aren't looking with your binoculars.

First stop will be the Skagit Wildlife Area Headquarters Unit (Wylie Slough) by 9am. At this stop: bathroom vault toilets, habitat sketching, quick General Impression of Size and Shape (GISS) sketching waterfowl, raptors, herons, or hunters.

Second stop will be Snow Goose Produce on Fir Island Road by 10:30am. They close for the season after the first weekend in October, but the parking lot is large. No shelter if weather is inclement. The surrounding fields and buildings may provide an opportunity for those interested in urban sketching. “Inktober” is a yearly October event with sketch prompts. Here is a link HOW TO INK — Inktober https://inktober.com/how-to-ink .

Third stop will be Padilla Bay open picnic shelter by noon on Bayview Edison Road across from Bay View State Park. At this stop: lunch, portable toilet, watercolor techniques with waterbrush, habitat and sea bird sketching.

We then continue north to our final stop by 2pm on Bayview Edison Road, taking a left on Samish Island Road (aka “the Samish T”). We will park at Skagit Wildlife Area (Samish Unit, aka “West 90”) by 2pm. No shelter if weather is inclement. Expect birders and hunters. Final “pit stop” at a hopefully adequate portable toilet.

We will then drive back east along the Samish Island Road past the “East 90” and slowly through the quaint town of Edison. We will continue along Bow Hill Road to join southbound I-5. We should return to Green Lake P&R no later than 5pm.

Expect cold, rainy, windy weather. We will not stop at coffee stands, so please pack what you'll need for the day. This is an accessible class trip with minimal walking.

Bring: A packed lunch (maybe warm soup?), water/drinks, a thermos of tea/coffee/cocoa, warm layers including hat and gloves and rain gear, and minimal portable sketch supplies (sketch book, pen, ink pen, and a portable palette and waterbrush if you watercolor). Carleen will have extra waterbrushes and a portable palette to share.

description:
REGISTER https://secure.birdsconnectsea.org/a/shape2026

Bird plumage often contains intricate details of color and pattern. But if the lighting is bad or the bird is far away, those details can be impossible to see. That's when we rely on shape. In this class we will compare the shapes of similar species to see how shape can help us make confident identifications under challenging conditions.

When you arrive, please look for the table tents with our event name on them (Birds Connect Seattle Board Game Night) or ask one of the friendly beertenders for assistance. description:

Corvids (jays, magpies, crows, and ravens) are among the most intelligent birds, displaying astounding feats of memory, problem-solving, and tool use. title: Conservation Reading Group: The Bird with the Flaming Red Feet
description:
REGISTER https://secure.birdsconnectsea.org/5jwG_kSJ-U-ORsuiGx0MzQ2

The Birds Connect Seattle Conservation Committee invites you to read and learn with us. Together, we'll deepen our understanding of conservation and become stronger advocates for birds and nature.

This quarter, we're reading The Bird with the Flaming Red Feet by Maria Mudd Ruth.

Purchase the book from our shop https://birdsconnectsea.myshopify.com/products/the-bird-with-flaming-red-feet-seasons-with-an-uncommonly-common-seabird , the proceeds of the sale will support conservation and other programs at Birds Connect Seattle.

Make sure to follow along on Addabook https://www.addabook.net/list/birdsconnect-L:ce309ad60c for prompts and reflections.

Book Description:

The Bird with Flaming Red Feet is a lively and heartfelt natural history of the Pigeon Guillemot, a charismatic seabird with a surprising story to tell. Found along the coast around the North Pacific and from Alaska to Southern California, this talkative and often-overlooked bird plays an outsized role in the health of marine ecosystem—earning its status as an "indicator species," especially for Washington's Puget Sound.

Author and longtime volunteer surveyor Maria Mudd Ruth weaves together science, field observation, and community storytelling in this engaging exploration of one bird's life. Drawing from over a decade of beachside study, she dives deep into the guillemot's behaviors, quirky traits, and ecological relationships. Along the way, readers meet the passionate citizen scientists who have built a unique community around caring for and studying this vibrant bird.

Bridging the gap between field guide and memoir, The Bird with Flaming Red Feet invites readers to slow down, look closely, and reconnect with the wild places—and creatures—just outside their door. It's a joyful call to observation, stewardship, and a deeper understanding of our coastal world.
